explanation: Showing the soles of your feet in Russia isn't treated as a serious insult the way it is in Thailand — it reads more as careless or inconsiderate, since feet are associated with street dirt. Propping your feet on furniture, armrests, or an opposite seat on public transport is the main thing locals object to.
local_tip: Keep your feet on the floor and off furniture or seats, especially if they'd be pointed toward another person.

also_check.note: The foot is the lowest part of the body, and pointing the sole at someone is a grave insult.
Showing the soles of your feet is generally not offensive, though it can read as very casual.
Showing the sole of your foot to someone is considered disrespectful, as the foot is seen as unclean.

sources.title: 5 Things NOT to do in Russia
